title: US History: Peoples to Present
subject: US History
description: A full-year journey through American history with primary sources and a documentary project each era.

milestones.title: First Peoples and early America
milestones.description: Indigenous civilizations before 1492 and the world they built.
milestones.projectIdea: Research one nation's governance, food, and trade; present as a museum-style exhibit card set.
milestones.resourceHint: Library books: Indigenous history of North America

milestones.title: Contact and colonization
milestones.description: Columbian exchange, motivations for colonization, and the thirteen colonies.
milestones.projectIdea: Colonial recruitment poster: design an ad convincing 1600s settlers to join your colony.

milestones.title: Road to revolution
milestones.description: Taxes, protests, and ideas of liberty from 1763 to 1776.
milestones.projectIdea: Debate: patriots vs loyalists — argue both sides in character.
milestones.resourceHint: Khan Academy: The road to revolution

milestones.title: Revolution and founding documents
milestones.description: The war, the Constitution, and the Bill of Rights.
milestones.projectIdea: Write your own Bill of Rights for a new settlement on Mars.

milestones.title: Early republic and expansion
milestones.description: Washington to Jackson; growth, conflict, and reform movements.
milestones.projectIdea: Timeline mural of westward expansion marking whose land it was at every step.

milestones.title: Sectionalism and Civil War
milestones.description: Causes, course, and consequences of the Civil War.
milestones.projectIdea: Letters home: write a week of correspondence from a fictional person on each side.

milestones.title: Reconstruction and its undoing
milestones.description: Reconstruction amendments, hope, backlash, and Jim Crow.
milestones.projectIdea: Analyze a Reconstruction-era primary source and present what it reveals.

milestones.title: Industrialization and immigration
milestones.description: Factories, cities, railroads, and the people who built them.
milestones.projectIdea: Family or local history: trace one immigrant story (yours or a neighbor's) through the era.

milestones.title: Progressive Era
milestones.description: Reformers, muckrakers, and the fights over who America is for.
milestones.projectIdea: Muckraker magazine: write an exposé (historical or modern) in the 1900s style.

milestones.title: World War I
milestones.description: America's path from neutrality to world power.
milestones.projectIdea: Propaganda analysis: compare WWI posters, then design an honest counter-poster.

milestones.title: Roaring Twenties and Great Depression
milestones.description: Boom, bust, and the New Deal.
milestones.projectIdea: Oral history: interview someone about hard economic times, then map it to the 1930s.

milestones.title: World War II
milestones.description: The home front and the world at war.
milestones.projectIdea: Build a 'home front museum box' of artifacts (real or recreated) with curator notes.

milestones.title: Cold War
milestones.description: Containment, conflict, and culture from 1945 to 1991.
milestones.projectIdea: Cold War timeline of one decade with a 'day in the life' diary entry.

milestones.title: Civil Rights Movement
milestones.description: The long freedom struggle and its leaders, strategy, and songs.
milestones.projectIdea: Freedom songs playlist with liner notes explaining each song's role in the movement.

milestones.title: Modern America
milestones.description: From the 1970s to today: technology, change, and ongoing debates.
milestones.projectIdea: Then and now photo essay: pair one historical image with one you take today on the same theme.
milestones.resourceHint: News archives: comparing coverage then and now

milestones.title: Capstone: History in the making
milestones.description: Synthesize the year: what threads run through all of American history?
milestones.projectIdea: Produce a 10-minute documentary (or podcast episode) on the thread you found.
milestones.resourceHint: Free video editors: CapCut or OpenShot
